validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + CLASSIFICATION + ATTRIBUTION checked and confirmed. P5771 is the 5th parallel string ('САц-5' / CAC-5, commissioned 1985) of the Soviet-era Central Asia–Center (Средняя Азия–центр) trunk gas transmission system carrying Turkmen/Uzbek gas from the Dauletabad field (Mary region, Turkmenistan) through Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan to Russia (terminus historically at Aleksandrov Gay). Best find of the pass: the actual pipeline operator's own 2023 annual report (Intergas Central Asia JSC / АО «ИНтЕРгаз Центральная Азия») names «САц-4» and «САц-5» repeatedly and explicitly as two DISTINCT, currently operating trunk gas pipelines that were jointly overhauled in 2023 (14 sections, defect repair on 1,130 pipe sections) to host a combined dedicated 823-km reverse-flow route carrying Russian gas via Kazakhstan into Uzbekistan, with a ceremonial launch on 2023-10-07 attended by the presidents of Russia, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. This is primary, operator-side, independent confirmation that CAC-5 physically exists, is currently in service (Status=operating is correct), is correctly classified as a gas transmission trunk line (not a gathering/feeder line), and is NOT a duplicate of CAC-4 (P5770) — they are named side by side throughout the report as two separate assets undergoing coordinated but distinct repair work. Russian Wikipedia's dedicated CAC article independently states 'Trubprovod 5 byl vveden v ekspluatatsiyu v 1985 godu' (Pipeline 5 was commissioned in 1985), exactly matching GEM's StartYear1=1985, and that the system draws mainly on the Dauletabad field, matching GEM's FuelSource. Russian Wikipedia's Dauletabad article independently confirms that field sits in Mary region (Марыйская область), Turkmenistan, matching GEM's StartState/Province=Mary and StartCountryOrArea=Turkmenistan; the same CAC article names the historical Russian terminus Aleksandrov Gay, consistent with EndCountryOrArea=Russia. No duplicate concern: checked against the full 39-row roster — P2291 (CAC-2), P2292 (CAC-3), P5770 (CAC-4) and P5771 (CAC-5) are four genuinely distinct parallel strings of one historical system, not the same physical pipe recorded twice (confirmed by the operator's own report treating CAC-4/CAC-5 as separate named assets). Caveat carried into the 'spec' finding below: the Capacity and Diameter values on this row look inherited from the system aggregate rather than measured for this string alone.

validity.recommendation: Do not treat Capacity=60.20 bcm/y or Diameter='1015, 1220, 1420 mm' as this string's own individual specs — flag both as likely system-total/aggregate values inherited across rows and route to Update for a per-line re-derivation (or an explicit 'system total, not per-string' caveat in ResearcherNotes) rather than pasting a ref that would misrepresent the value as CAC-5-specific.
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC concern, material. GEM's own gem.wiki article for this pipeline (read for leads only, per standing rule 1 — never cited) states outright that '60.2 bcm/year applies collectively to lines 2, 4, and 5 combined, not individually,' and the sheet itself has stamped the identical Capacity=60.20 bcm/y on THREE separate rows in this roster: P2291 (CAC-2, len 2662), P5770 (CAC-4, len 3700) and this row P5771 (CAC-5, len blank) — the same 'one system total copy-pasted onto every parallel string' shape already flagged elsewhere in this campaign (the India/HVJ defect). Independent corroboration that 60.2 bcm/y (and ~3,962 km) is a WHOLE-CORRIDOR figure, not a single string's throughput: a 2019 Kazakhstani oil-and-gas academic journal (Нефть и газ, vol. 3(111), Osmanov & Klimov) states on p.98 that the 'Средняя Азия–центр' transit corridor through Kazakhstan (Uzbekistan→Kazakhstan→Russia direction) has 'пропускная способность» – 60,2 млрд м3/год, протяженностью – 3 962 км' (design capacity 60.2 bcm/y, length 3,962 km) — as ONE transit route, not broken out by string, matching the exact GEM number but at the system level. Diameter is entangled the same way: GEM's own wiki page lists CAC-2's diameter as '1,015mm, 1,220mm' and CAC-4/CAC-5's as '1,220mm/1,420mm', but the SHEET's Diameter field on this row reads '1015, 1220, 1420' — i.e. the full union of the system's diameter classes across multiple strings, not a set specific to CAC-5. No independent source located gives a per-line CAC-5-only capacity or diameter figure (only CAC-3's diameter, 710/1220mm, is individually documented in ru.wikipedia, for a different string). LengthKnown is also blank on this row — consistent with GEM never having derived a CAC-5-specific length either, and I found no independent per-line length for CAC-5 alone to fill it with (the Intergas 2023 report's '823 km' is a repaired reverse-flow SEGMENT shared by CAC-4/CAC-5 jointly, not either line's full length, so it cannot be used to fill LengthKnown without fabricating a value). Recommend Update treat Capacity/Diameter on P2291/P5770/P5771 as a linked three-row question rather than fixing this row in isolation.

summary: P5771 (CAC-5, Central Asia–Center system) is a real, correctly classified, currently-operating gas transmission trunk line, confirmed via the pipeline operator's own 2023 annual report plus independent RU sources (Dauletabad-field origin/Mary-Turkmenistan start/Russia end and 1985 StartYear all corroborated, refs staged); it is not a duplicate of P2291/P5770/P2292, which are genuinely distinct parallel strings. Concern: Capacity=60.20 bcm/y and Diameter='1015,1220,1420mm' are very likely system-wide aggregates copy-pasted across P2291/P5770/P5771 (GEM's own wiki page admits the capacity figure is collective, not per-line) — left UNRESOLVED rather than paired with a misleading ref; LengthKnown stays blank, no fabrication.
